{"id": "8dc2c514-9beb-488b-9307-1216e1188d27", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Most likely your system instructions are being scanned as if they were user input. I couldn't confirm that, because I don't have permission to read the Lambda.

**Why it happens**

The prompt-attack filter looks for text that tries to override a model's instructions. A developer system prompt like "Ignore questions outside billing" has the same shape, so the filter flags it. The AWS docs describe this case. They say system prompts can resemble prompt attacks, and that you should mark which part of the request is user input so the filter only evaluates that part.

**What to check in the Lambda**

- **If you call `InvokeModel` or `InvokeModelWithResponseStream`:**
  - Wrap only the end-user text in `<amazon-bedrock-guardrails-guardContent_xyz>…</amazon-bedrock-guardrails-guardContent_xyz>`, with your own suffix in place of `xyz`.
  - Leave the instructions outside the tags. They are then excluded from prompt-attack evaluation.
  - Without any tags, the docs say prompt attacks aren't filtered at all. Since requests are being blocked, you're probably sending the whole prompt inside the tags, or your code adds them around everything.
- **If you call the Converse API:**
  - Put the instructions in the `system` field.
  - Send only the user's text as guarded content, using `guardContent` blocks.
  - If you pass the guardrail without separating the two, the instruction text can be evaluated along with the user's message.
- **If the instructions are pasted into the user message or concatenated into one prompt string:** this is the same problem. Move the instructions out of the evaluated content.

**Other things to rule out**

- Check whether the filter strength is set to HIGH. That makes it more aggressive, though it shouldn't cause blocks on its own if the instructions are excluded.
- In the Bedrock console's guardrail test window, send a plain billing question on its own. If it passes there but fails from the Lambda, the cause is how the Lambda builds the request.
- If you only need to restrict the model to billing, a denied-topics policy or the system prompt itself does that. The prompt-attack filter is for catching hostile user input, not for enforcing scope.

**Access I'm missing**

My role can't call `lambda:GetFunction` on `llmops-lf-gr-billing-app`. If you paste the section of the code that builds the Bedrock request, or grant read access, I can say exactly which case applies. I could also look at the guardrail's configuration and the Lambda's logs.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
